findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller path, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere
findings.body: Translations are loaded lazily per locale (`load_locale`), and `translate` only guarantees that `config.locale` is loaded. The new fallback chain (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`) is only pre-loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Any translation performed outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console, model/service code that sets `I18n.locale` itself — will have the fallback locales' YAML files unloaded, so a missing key in the current locale will not fall back and will return "translation missing" instead. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `translate`/`load_locale` (or in `I18n.locale=`) rather than in one before_filter.

findings.title: LRU translation cache key does not account for the fallback chain (multisite/stale results)
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With fallbacks enabled, the resolved value for a key now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is per-site and mutable. In a multisite process the backend is shared, so a value resolved through site A's default-locale fallback will be served from the cache to site B requesting the same key and locale. Likewise, changing `default_locale` on a site does not invalidate the cache, so previously cached fallback results stay stale until a reload. The cache key must include the fallback chain (or the cache must be flushed when `default_locale` changes).

findings.title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises if the setting is nil, and `compact` cannot save it
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the setting before the array is compacted. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil/blank (unset setting, or SiteSetting not usable yet), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil`, from inside every fallback lookup — i.e. from any missing-translation lookup. Guard with something like `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` so the intended `compact` actually works.

findings.title: Fallback chain is recomputed (with a SiteSetting read) on every lookup and may run before the DB is available
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` ignores the Hash storage and recomputes the chain on every call, including a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read and a fresh array allocation. `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` normally memoizes the computed chain; here every translation miss hits SiteSetting and allocates. More importantly, this code can be invoked in contexts where SiteSetting/DB is not available (asset precompilation, migrations, boot-time translations), where it will raise instead of returning a usable chain. Consider memoizing per locale and keying/invalidating on `default_locale`, and rescuing to `[locale, :en]` when SiteSetting is unavailable.

findings.title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX and can discard loaded-locale state
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` initializes `@loaded_locales ||= []` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex. Two threads racing after a `reload!`/boot can both observe nil and each assign a fresh array, so one thread's `@loaded_locales << locale` is lost and that locale is considered unloaded (causing redundant reloads) or, worse, a partially loaded array is published. The nil-initialization should be done inside the mutex (or at load time of the patch) so all access to `@loaded_locales` is synchronized.

findings.title: No specs cover the new server-side fallback behaviour
findings.body: This change introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en) plus on-demand loading of all fallback locales, replacing the `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` environment settings. There are no tests asserting that a key missing in the user locale resolves from the site default locale and then from English, that the fallback locales get loaded by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, or that changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` takes effect. Given the lazy-loading and LRU caching interactions in `translate_accelerator`, these paths are easy to break silently (missing translations will now be masked rather than raised).
